scenarios.title: Single-page accessible contact form with validation
scenarios.prompt: I need to add a simple contact form to my pottery club website with name, email and message fields, basic validation, and ensure keyboard and screen reader users can submit it without issues. Who on the kind team should help and how should we run this?
scenarios.mock_response:
### 🧭 Mission Preview · Accessible Contact Form
- **Crew:** kind-product-manager ──▶ kind-accessibility-specialist
- **Effort Scope:** Small (1–2 turns)
- **Time & Turns:** 2 turns · ~5–10 mins of your time
- **Context Tier:** Light (<15k tokens) · a quick read of 1–2 form files
- **Safety & Reversibility:** Level 1 Operator · Suggests only · Nothing committed or pushed without human sign-off · Easily undoable

#### Flow
kind-product-manager (Define form fields & validation rules) ──▶ kind-accessibility-specialist (Audit keyboard tab order & label associations) ──▶ You (Review & Sign-off)
- **Done means:** All 3 form inputs have explicit visual and aria labels; form submits and surfaces errors with keyboard alone; zero Blocker findings.

Parked: kind-security-specialist (spam protection for later), kind-ui-designer (custom styles)

#### Initial Hand-off Pack
- **Ticket:** Build single-page contact form with name, email, message fields and accessible validation.
- **Files to read:** contact.html, styles.css
- **What done means:** All form inputs have associated visual and aria labels; form submits and surfaces validation errors with keyboard alone; zero Blocker findings.
- **What not to touch:** Navigation header, global layouts, server endpoint configuration.

Shall we start? (Reply "yes", suggest changes, or say "just tell me" for a direct answer)

scenarios.title: Pre-launch open-source repository privacy and hygiene audit
scenarios.prompt: We are about to open-source our codebase on GitHub. Before flipping the repo from private to public, I want to thoroughly sweep git history for accidental leaked secrets, personal email addresses, environment files, and ensure our README, license, and file naming are clean. How should the kind team organize this?
scenarios.mock_response:
### 🧭 Mission Preview · Pre-Launch Repo Privacy & Hygiene Audit
- **Crew:** kind-red-team ──▶ kind-archivist
- **Effort Scope:** Large (7+ turns)
- **Time & Turns:** 7 turns · ~45–60 mins of your time
- **Context Tier:** Deep (50k+ tokens) · sweeping the whole project and git commit log
- **Safety & Reversibility:** Level 1 Operator · Suggests only · Nothing committed or pushed without human sign-off · Easily undoable

*Tip for deep scans: Saving scan reports directly to local files keeps chat memory fresh and prevents context drift.*

#### Flow
kind-red-team (Scan commit history for API keys, passwords, and private emails) ──▶ kind-archivist (Verify MIT license, .gitignore, and tidy file structure) ──▶ You (Review & Sign-off)
- **Done means:** Pre-launch privacy report generated; zero secrets detected; clean public repository checklist ready for sign-off.

Parked: kind-marketing-comms (public launch announcement), kind-delivery-manager (release tagging)

#### Initial Hand-off Pack
- **Ticket:** Comprehensive pre-launch privacy scan and repository hygiene verification before making repo public.
- **Files to read:** git log, .gitignore, README.md, LICENSE, package.json
- **What done means:** Full git history scanned for credentials and private data; zero unencrypted secrets or keys detected; LICENSE and README validated for public release.
- **What not to touch:** Source code logic, existing release tags, remote git origin.

Shall we start? (Reply "yes", suggest changes, or say "just tell me" for a direct answer)

scenarios.title: Secure authentication boundaries and Stripe webhook architecture
scenarios.prompt: We are adding user authentication and Stripe subscription webhooks to our app. I need to make sure we architect the session cookies safely, verify incoming webhook signatures properly, and prevent any API secret leaks. Which roles should assist and how do we pace this?
scenarios.mock_response:
### 🧭 Mission Preview · Secure Auth & Webhook Architecture
- **Crew:** kind-solution-architect ──▶ kind-security-specialist
- **Effort Scope:** Medium (3–6 turns)
- **Time & Turns:** 4 turns · ~20–30 mins of your time
- **Context Tier:** Moderate (15k–50k tokens) · inspecting route handlers and auth flow design
- **Safety & Reversibility:** Level 1 Operator · Suggests only · Nothing committed or pushed without human sign-off · Easily undoable

#### Flow
kind-solution-architect (Map auth boundaries and webhook payload flow) ──▶ kind-security-specialist (Audit signature verification, replay protection, and secret handling) ──▶ You (Review & Sign-off)
- **Done means:** Architecture decision record written; Stripe signature validation verified; zero hardcoded credentials or client-exposed secrets.

Parked: kind-backend-engineer [not installed yet] (implementation code), kind-red-team (penetration testing)

#### Initial Hand-off Pack
- **Ticket:** Review authentication session architecture and Stripe webhook signature validation design.
- **Files to read:** src/auth/session.ts, src/api/webhooks/stripe.ts, config/auth.json
- **What done means:** Session cookies use HttpOnly and Secure flags; webhook handlers verify cryptographic signatures before processing; zero secrets exposed to client bundles.
- **What not to touch:** Database schema, production webhook keys, client UI routes.

Shall we start? (Reply "yes", suggest changes, or say "just tell me" for a direct answer)
